quests.title: Every Aspect of a Warrior

dialogue.t: Why must I persist? Why can't I just give up...? Forget it, I give up! Help me, Manyoya.
What an embarrassment! Stop acting like a child and giving up whenever things don't go smoothly. How can you even call yourself a warrior? I'm ashamed to call you my brother.
And are you telling me you've never been stumped and needed help?
I have, which is why I'm here to get Father and Manyoya's opinions on the fruits of my special training. I'm not a coward like you!
Acomitl, I believe the captain rejected your resignation so that you could give it more thought. Don't make important decisions in the heat of things.
Calm down and make your own choice. The most important thing is that you don't come to regret it.
I'm retired, and even I don't know what the future holds for me, so I fear I haven't the right to give you any guidance.
Whoa! So you three are siblings!
It's you two!?
My apologies, dear benefactor. My escape plan fell through.
Is there no way for me to escape this pain? Being a warrior is so exhausting. Why can't everything be simpler?
Still preoccupied with thoughts of the flying squad?
I'm sorry, Acomitl. Based on my experience, things don't get simpler that way.
Still, I just finished repairing Matahga's arm guards. Manyoya, do yours's need any work? Hmm? We have guests.
Ah, they're adventurers we met during our training away from home, father. They even helped Acomitl out.
Then greetings, kind friends. I'm Xueyoni, a training master and their father.
Acomitl seems to be in terrible condition, so let us know if you need help.
Thank you for the offer, but I think Acomitl is completely fine.
Huh? You intend to just leave him be?
Haha! What I'm trying to say is... Let's put it this way. You're adventurers, so you must have joined the Adventurers' Guild, right?
Now that's an amazing organization. You adventurers desire to explore the world, right?
Even so, I imagine every adventurer has their motivations. Some explore for the money, others desire knowledge, and some are just bored of doing nothing.
So, it's a most impressive feat the Adventurers' Guild has achieved in uniting all those people under one banner.

Take me for example. I'm an old man who retired after serving as a Saurian rider in the flying squad and went on to become a master trainer in our tribe. Yet, I cannot imagine what a Guild containing the master trainers of all six tribes would look like.
Uh... What does that have to do with Acomitl?
That's how our father explains things. Back when he was still in the flying squad, everyone there, even the Qucusaurs, would willingly hear his opinion.
He's now a master trainer for our tribe, and anyone who wishes to become a warrior comes to seek his advice, so relax — just listen for now.
Heh, that's all in the past, Manyoya. But I shall finish the tale all the same.
We master trainers aspire toward the ideal of the "warrior." That's what inspires us to take the time and effort to design and set our training programs up.
We all have a "dream warrior" we wish to see emerge, but no single person can dictate what such a warrior should be.
We master trainers have found agreeing on any principles and regulations impossible, let alone forming a Guild.
That "greatest warrior" has countless faces and personalities.
They are strong-willed at times, but they sometimes struggle with self-doubt — not to mention how they will age and die.
Must warriors be immune to burnout? I can show you multiple woven scrolls that show how self-doubt and exhaustion plague everyone equally.
Must warriors be huge? I know of many who looked like giants yet were despicable beyond compare. Such are recorded upon woven scrolls too.
And of course, warriors will decline, as the law of nature dictates.
My kids call me a warrior, but look at me. I'm an old bird who doesn't fly anymore — I've no strength for it.
A warrior with a perfect face, a person who conforms to every boring standard, will not be recognized as a hero here in Natlan.
Manyoya, Acomitl, Matahga, I've brought you here, for you are to be the heroes of the Flower-Feather Clan, gazing down from a great height.
Your worries and desires are fleeting states on a hero's long journey, not problems that need solving.
Does leaving the flying squad mean one is no longer a warrior? Does joining the flying squad automatically make one a warrior? There are no such things.
It's okay to have ambitions, to hesitate, and to feel lost. You are a warrior, and a warrior must undergo trials to become a hero.
Accept how you are now, learn to live with that state, and overcome it. Never let it control you.
This is the way of Natlan — the way of heroes. Do you understand?
I understand, Father.
Acomitl, are you still hesitating?
Constant lectures aren't our family's way. Go fly with your brother and sister, just like when you were little.
Let your mind and body help you decide. Staying cooped up in the house and overthinking things won't lead to any good.
I got it, Father.
Do Master Trainers always speak so abstractly? Paimon didn't really get any of it. Did you, {NICKNAME}?

dialogue.sit: Yep. Basically, this will involve a Gliding Challenge.
Nope. Family upbringing techniques are too profound.

dialogue.t: Adventurer, I've heard about you from my kids. You're a fascinating young person.
Having the guts to compete with Manyoya, help little Acomitl... and you even gained Matahga's recognition — a true warrior, you are.
I'd like to invite you to fly with these kids. How about it?
Haha, alright. When you've decided, come over and let us know.
All three of my kids are top-tier fliers in the Flower-Feather Clan. You'll have a great time flying together.
Come and fly with my kids, young one. It's not every day you get to compete with the Flower-Feather Clan's finest.
Chase after the <color=#00E1FFFF>flying torch</color> on the course. Whoever catches it first wins. That's how I trained them when they were little.
<color=#00E1FFFF>The torch is held by a balloon decorated with red feathers</color>, symbolizing the responsibility and honor that a warrior should bear. I made it for them.
You'll recognize it once you see it. So, are you up for the contest?

dialogue.sit: I need a little more time.

dialogue.t: Haha, great! Let's head to the starting point and get ready then.
Another race? Haha! Just wait and see!
You're pretty confident. C'mon, Acomitl. We can't lose here!
Losing to you is whatever, but there's no way I'm losing to Matahga!
{NICKNAME}, be sure to give it your all, too. Don't fall for Matahga's late-game pushes. He's been doing that for ages.
When you're ready, let my father know, and we'll fly together.
Not bad, young one! Hahahaha!
But you'll need more practice if you want to surpass my kids. Don't take it too hard, though! It's rare for anyone to achieve success in one go.
If you want to try again, just come find me.
Not bad, young one! Hahahaha!
But you'll need more practice if you want to surpass my kids. Don't take it too hard, though! It's rare for anyone to achieve success in one go.
If you want to try again, just come find me.
Haha! Sorry, but I pulled ahead this time!
Gah, Matahga, you annoying little... You've been like this since forever, always going all out in the second half!
Feeling bitter? Catch me if you can, then! Haha!
You flew well, young one!
How was my flying just now?
Thanks for your encouragement, but I can tell you're still a cut above.
Acomitl...
It's not what you think. I'm not discouraged because I can't outdo others. I can fly, I know I can.
Still, being in bad form for so long has ruined my self-confidence. I just can't approach flying with any sense of calm.
{NICKNAME}'s different. His(Her) posture is way more relaxed. Anyone with eyes can see that.
Father, I know that you and sis want me to make up my own mind and not avoid the issue.
But if I told you now, that whether it's my body, my brain, or my heart...
That they all refuse to continue on a path that's not meant for me... Would you still support me?
It's okay, so long as it's your own decision, and you're willing to shoulder the consequences.
Matahga, will you...
Hey! I'm not going to criticize you at a time like this. I've always known the sort of person you are, Big Brother.
If you can't handle this, then just make a decisive break with it. As long as you stay true to yourself, you remain a warrior. No one has the right to criticize you.
Sometimes, the job of a Master Trainer is quite easy. I make training plans for warriors, but I don't have to take part myself.
However, I, too, once flew around with Saurians day in and day out, and I know the true face of that kind of life.
Criticizing others is easy. Taking action is always harder.
As a trainer, I suggest you request time off to recuperate both physically and mentally, even if it leads to dissatisfaction within the team.
As your father, I know you don't want to continue, and I respect that choice.
No longer being part of the flying squad isn't the end of the world. The warriors of the Flower-Feather Clan don't have to prove their worth through flying alone.
Thank you... I was worried you'd...
Don't overthink it. We're your family, and we'll always help you find a way, no matter what.
Being a warrior sure is tough! Paimon never imagined it would be this hard to join the Flower-Feather Clan's flying squad.

dialogue.sit: Not everyone can be a warrior.

dialogue.t: Ooh, that's right! Thinking about all the things we've encountered along the way, we've overcome them all. That's something we can be proud of, eh?
And if becoming a warrior isn't easy in itself, growing from a warrior into a hero is even more so.
I've seen enough of the former to know when someone possesses the qualities needed to become the latter.
You have undergone many trials, haven't you, youngster? I can see it in your eyes.
It seems I wasn't mistaken. Your path differs from ours, and you might still have a ways to go. I'd be happy to assist a future hero.
What's more, you've met and helped our family.
If you want to use the training course here, just let me know. You can take off from here anytime.
Don't mention it. If anything, I'm eager to witness the moment you become a hero, resplendent in the skies.
Aw, I lost again. Even after all that practice, I still lost to him(her).
I told you this ages ago. There's no end to thinking about winning. Gotta admire your drive to just charge ahead without fear, though.
Well, you were like that when you were younger, too, following behind me every day, talking about how you wanted to become a master Saurian tamer...
Quit teasing me, sis...
You are all good children of mine, and fine warriors, too — and all warriors must face different challenges at different points...
Which is fine. So long as your consciences are clear, I am proud of you.

quests.description: “What we trainers pursue, myself included, isn’t success…”
